title: Extract the Socket.IO auth middleware into a named, testable function
description: server/index.js:274-308 defines `io.use(async (socket, next) => {...})` as an anonymous inline function — untestable in isolation without a real socket.io-client handshake (not currently a devDependency; adding one just for this is heavier than the alternative). Extract the exact same body into a named, exported function `socketAuthMiddleware(socket, next)` (pure behavior extraction, zero logic change — same token extraction from handshake.auth.token or Authorization header, same verifyToken call, same ban-check try/catch, same next(new Error(...)) calls), keep `io.use(socketAuthMiddleware)` at the call site, and add `module.exports.socketAuthMiddleware = socketAuthMiddleware` (or fold into the existing `module.exports = { app, server, startServer }` line) so it can be required directly in a test without spinning up a real server.

title: Add Jest unit coverage for socketAuthMiddleware's fail-closed behavior
description: Closes the 'never fail-open a socket JWT check' gap flagged in server-invariants.mdc — currently zero coverage anywhere for the Socket.IO connection-auth path (messagesAuth.test.js only covers the HTTP POST /api/messages route, a separate code path). Mock '@clerk/backend' (jest.mock('@clerk/backend', () => ({ verifyToken: jest.fn() }))) and './utils/auth' / './utils/admin' as needed (clerkClient.users.getUser, resolveIsBanned) — do not hit real Clerk. Require { socketAuthMiddleware } from '../index' (this now works without booting the HTTP server, per step 1's export). Build a minimal mock `socket` object ({ handshake: { auth: {}, headers: {} } }) per test case and a jest.fn() `next` spy. Cover: (1) no token at all (empty handshake.auth and no Authorization header) -> next called with an Error whose message is 'Unauthorized', socket.userId never set; (2) a token present but verifyToken rejects (invalid/expired) -> next called with an Unauthorized error, not re-thrown; (3) verifyToken resolves but claims.sub is falsy/missing -> next called with Unauthorized; (4) a valid token with claims.sub set, and the Clerk ban-check (clerkClient.users.getUser) itself throwing -> connection still succeeds (next called with no arguments) per the code's explicit intent ('Clerk lookup failure shouldn't block a socket that already has a valid JWT') — this is the one deliberate non-fail-closed branch, and the test should assert it stays that way, not accidentally regress to blocking; (5) a valid token where the ban check succeeds and resolveIsBanned returns true -> next called with an Error 'Account suspended', not a generic Unauthorized (distinguish the two paths). Every case must assert socket.userId's exact final state, not just whether next() has an error argument.

title: Add a Jest test proving Game+ChatRoom creation actually rolls back, not just 'both exist on success'
description: server-invariants.mdc's transaction rule says Game+ChatRoom pairing 'must happen in the same interactive transaction' — existing tests (gameRoster.test.js etc.) confirm the ChatRoom exists after a successful create, but none exercise the actual atomicity property: does a failure inside the transaction (server/services/gameService.js:855-908) roll back the already-created Game row too? Note: jest.spyOn(prisma.chatRoom, 'create') does NOT work here — Prisma's $transaction callback receives a distinct `tx` client, not the top-level `prisma` object, so spying on the outer client misses every write made through `tx` (verified by running it: the spy never fired, game was created successfully despite the mock). Use a real constraint violation instead: POST /api/games with `invitedParticipantIds: ['<a user id that does not exist>']` — the nested Participation/ChatParticipant create trips a genuine foreign-key violation inside the transaction, which is not P2002 so createGroupChatForGame's catch doesn't swallow it, and the transaction genuinely aborts. Assert the response is not 2xx, then assert prisma.game.findFirst({ where: { title: <the unique test title used> } }) returns null. Fixtures/mocks follow gameRoster.test.js's pattern (user.upsert + field.create, jest.mock('../utils/auth')).
